root_cause.text: `mt7925_mac_write_txwi_80211()` in the mt76/mt7925 Wi-Fi driver accessed management-frame action fields without first validating that the `skb` was long enough, allowing an out-of-bounds read on short action frames.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `skb->len >= IEEE80211_MIN_ACTION_SIZE + 1` before reading `mgmt->u.action.category` and `mgmt->u.action.u.addba_req.action_code`, and the commit message explicitly says it fixes a “possible oob access” by “Check[ing] frame length before accessing the mgmt fields in mt7925_mac_write_txwi_80211.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a minimum-length guard before parsing action frames to prevent invalid memory access.
intent_record.what: A new length check was added to the conditional in mt7925_mac_write_txwi_80211(): `skb->len >= IEEE80211_MIN_ACTION_SIZE + 1` is now required before matching the action frame as a BACK category ADDBA request.
intent_record.how: This prevents the code from reading action-frame fields unless the skb is large enough to contain them, avoiding out-of-bounds access on short or malformed management frames and only classifying valid ADDBA requests as such.

grouping_result.intent: Add a minimum-length guard before parsing action frames to prevent invalid memory access.

This accesses a deeper action subfield from the skb without a minimum-length guard, making it vulnerable to out-of-bounds reads on short action frames.
